name: The cause of a rule (ʿilla)
definition: The reason the grammarians give for a rule: why a word takes the ending or form it takes.
body: Al-Zajjājī, in al-Īḍāḥ fī ʿilal al-naḥw, sorted the causes into three degrees. The teaching cause (ʿilla taʿlīmiyya) is the one a student needs: zaydun is in rafʿ because it is the doer. The analogical cause (qiyāsiyya) asks why the doer is in rafʿ at all, and the speculative cause (jadaliyya naẓariyya) asks why it took rafʿ and not naṣb; later books call these the first, second and third causes.

The causes were a pride of the Basran school and a target of its critics. Ibn Maḍāʾ asked the grammarians to keep the first cause and drop the second and third, since they explain nothing a speaker needs. In the commentaries the word appears constantly: 'the ʿilla of its being mabnī is its likeness to the particle'.

examples.text: Zayd struck ʿAmr: why is zaydun in rafʿ? Because it is the doer (the first cause); why the doer in rafʿ? To tell it from the object (the second); why rafʿ and not naṣb? Because the doer is one and the objects many, and the heavier vowel went to the fewer (a third cause given by the grammarians).
